dedupe_keys.name: flood fragility and loss data for wood frame building components multi variate and single variable approaches

description: This dataset gives component-level parameters for flood fragility and loss models of wood-frame residential buildings, supporting a paper that compares multi-variate (flood depth and duration) and single-variable approaches. It was deposited on Mendeley Data in 2020 by John van de Lindt and co-authors. For each building component it lists the mean and standard deviation of resistance to flood depth and duration with upper and lower bounds, and assigns components to damage states; resistances come from earlier work by van de Lindt and Taggart, experiments by Aglan and stated engineering judgement. It also gives the minimum, maximum and mean replacement cost of each component, compiled from U.S. contractor cost sources such as HomeAdvisor, HomeGuides and UpCodes, and the resulting replacement cost of each damage state. Coverage: typical U.S. wood-frame houses. Access: open download from Mendeley Data. Licence: public domain dedication; free. Caveats: some resistances are engineering judgement, and costs are web-sourced national ranges. Simulation uses are building-level flood damage and loss modelling, including duration effects, in community resilience tools. Related records: IN-CORE and the Hurricane Harvey and Ian repair permits.
